blocks.label: on being coached by his father
blocks.text: I think it has gone pretty well, to be honest, this first year with just my dad. Everything has worked for both of us. Obviously, it's not easy when he has to travel every week, but it has worked. As I always say, I don't see any reason to change anything. But I also have to say that we have one month to think about the things we can improve for next season. I'm super grateful for everything he has done for me. So we'll have time in December to talk about those topics, but I'm not sure what's going to happen next year yet.

blocks.label: on his fighting spirit this season
blocks.text: I've given everything on court in every match I've played this season. That is something I'm very proud of: not giving up in any match.

blocks.label: after his win over Medvedev
blocks.text: I think I did everything well. I think I just hit the ball in the sweet spot.

blocks.label: on the hamstring scare vs Medvedev
blocks.text: Well, I feel it a little bit. I'm not going to lie. I was playing really well and suddenly I felt a little problem in my hamstring. But it's just something minor. I mean, I could play really good tennis from that moment until the end of the match. I didn't want to push too much to the limit, I was a break up at that point, so I just tried to hold my serve, play calmly, smoothly, relaxed and simply enjoy it. I was trying to stay relaxed, to move not too aggressively. Right now I'm just feeling OK. We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow are really going to be important days ahead of me.

blocks.label: on still playing good tennis despite the problem
blocks.text: I had some minor physical problems during the match. But I think everyone saw that I was still able to play good tennis and move well around the court.

blocks.label: on knowing his body from Past experience
blocks.text: These are moments I have already experienced. I'm getting to know my body better. The fact that I have already gone through these situations several times helps me react correctly both on the court and off it.

blocks.label: on what it takes to play Medvedev
blocks.text: When it comes to playing against Medvedev, you have to be chill. You have to be relaxed, because a lot of balls come again and again and again. You have to accept it. That's what I did well today, because it let me think clearly and think pretty well in some really tough moments that I had today.

blocks.label: on his return against Medvedev
blocks.text: I would say the return. I returned really well. On the second serve, I returned really aggressively, really, really well, really deep.

blocks.label: after his win over Jodar
blocks.text: I knew it wasn't going to be an easy match going in. I was happy that I was able to get through some tough moments in the first set. Early on I was down break points, and I was able to hold serve and get to that tiebreaker. Once I was in the tiebreaker I felt confident, fending off those set points and coming through it in the end. It was a tricky second set as well, being up a break and losing it, but I thought I fought well and competed well.

blocks.label: on his semi-final hopes and Fritz vs Zverev
blocks.text: I'm always rooting for him. I think him and Sasha are going to have a great match. I think if he takes Sasha out in straights, he gets through to the semi-finals. I'm looking forward to it either way. I think both those guys are great guys. I'd love to make the semi-finals here for the first time. I did my job today, and let's see what happens.

blocks.label: on Jodar qualifying for Turin in his debut season
blocks.text: Rafa is one of the best young talents that tennis has seen in a long time. To be here playing in Turin in his first year on tour, starting the year outside of the top 100, is a ridiculous feat. So I hope all you guys recognize how special that is.

blocks.label: on his aggressive game and improved baseline play
blocks.text: I'm trying to be smart in the decisions I make. I still play very aggressively. I pay attention above all to my footwork and I try to take the ball early. I think that when I manage to win the long rallies and come out of them without making wrong decisions or committing unforced errors, that's where opponents struggle the most against me. When I step on court, everyone knows I have a big serve. But if opponents think, OK, I just have to get a few balls back in play and then Ben will miss, it becomes much easier for them to take control and feel comfortable in the rally. When instead the opponent feels he has to do something special to beat me, with the way I'm able to move and cover the court now, which is much better than before, it becomes harder for him to find solutions. So I try to stay true to my identity, play aggressively and come to the net when I can. All this without falling apart from the baseline.

blocks.label: on adapting to the ATP Finals and his return
blocks.text: It's not a tournament where you arrive and immediately feel at ease. This year I changed my mindset on the return.

blocks.label: on hiring Juan Carlos Ferrero as coach
blocks.text: The reason that we brought him on is for a different philosophy from the tennis perspective, the experience that he has from a coaching perspective and a playing perspective. I think there are so many improvements I can make on the other surfaces, with my groundstrokes, technically, strategically as well. From what I can see in a small amount of time, I think it'll work very well. I think the great thing is that, outside of a tennis perspective, the philosophy is similar to my dad's in how they approach the game, the type of people they are. With the little amount of time I've spent with Juan Carlos, things have become pretty clear: the type of guy he is, the character that he has, the non-negotiables in terms of attitude. There are so many things that go hand in hand with my dad as well. So that part is easy.

blocks.label: after his win over Cobolli
blocks.text: Just fighting. Like, I felt like after I got the break back, I was a better player in the set. And he did a good job of fighting, came up with some goods. I ended up playing a good breaker, and I wanted to get on him early in the second.

blocks.label: on playing with the crowd against him
blocks.text: Every time I play out here, it's an experience. It was packed today again, and fans against me, we played some crazy points. I'm not used to it being that one-sided, but it's cool, man.

blocks.label: on the long rally against Cobolli
blocks.text: We're both running side to side, and I was like, I'm just going to bear down, and he's going to have to lace a winner.

blocks.label: on facing Medvedev next
blocks.text: I'm going to have to take it from him. He's going to make me earn it. He's going to make me execute at the highest level, and if I do that, I like my chances. If I don't, he'll get it done. So it's pretty much that simple.

blocks.label: on his plan for the next match
blocks.text: In the next match I plan to be very aggressive. The court is getting a little bit faster.

blocks.label: after his loss to Alcaraz
blocks.text: Of course, it's not easy to play Carlos when he's full of confidence. To be able to beat him, you need to play a perfect or near-perfect game, which I didn't manage to do, and I lost. I should have been more competitive on serve.

blocks.label: on whether faster courts help against Alcaraz
blocks.text: I still think the reality is that the faster the surface, the easier it is and the more chances you have to beat Carlos. But look, he wins a lot of matches, and it doesn't matter which surface. He's basically won all four Grand Slams, so it doesn't matter whether it's slow or fast.

blocks.label: on how to counter Alcaraz
blocks.text: To counter Alcaraz you have to take away his time.

blocks.label: on facing Medvedev at the ATP Finals
blocks.text: I'm gonna have to take it from him. He's gonna make me earn it. He's gonna make me execute at the highest level, and if I do that, I like my chances. If I don't, he'll get it done. It's pretty much that simple.

blocks.label: on Alcaraz's level in their Turin match
blocks.text: There are moments when he's definitely Superman and plays pretty crazy.

blocks.label: after his win over Shelton
blocks.text: The first set was almost perfect … That helps when two big servers are playing each other … In the second-set tiebreak I played a few fantastic points, especially the match point was the highlight.

blocks.label: on his match-point forehand pass
blocks.text: I don't care how I win the match point as long as I win it. But I think it was definitely a highlight a little bit. But funny enough, I was very clear-minded of what I wanted to do with that ball, and it was perfect.

blocks.label: on not knowing he needed straight sets
blocks.text: No, I didn't know that, but I think for me, if I focus on myself and I play good tennis, the results will take care of themselves in a way. … It's about playing good tennis, and I feel like I did that today. I did that against Rafa two days ago, and that's the outcome of it.

blocks.label: after his loss to Fils
blocks.text: The first set, I think it was a competitive match, because both of us were playing a high level of tennis, but then my tennis and obviously physically I dropped a little bit. When you drop your level here, your opponent is not going to drop it.

blocks.label: on his physical struggles against Fils
blocks.text: I'm better now, but it was tough obviously, because I felt that I couldn't compete and physically, I wasn't at the level today, especially in the last two sets.

blocks.label: on the experience gap with established opponents
blocks.text: These players have been playing here on Tour for five, six, seven years, so they are used to this. Every match is different. If you are not competitive, if you don't have the right mindset or mentality to approach the match, it's very difficult to compete against these types of guys.

blocks.label: on his debut season on Tour
blocks.text: It wasn't meant to be at the end of the second set, but I think when I'm more on Tour, I'll learn more things, but as this first year, I'm happy with how the season has gone for me. However, it's my first season on Tour, so I was new. I didn't know what I was going to face and what we could expect in the first season. But I'm super proud of the work I've done. I've given everything on court in every match that I've played this season.

blocks.label: on hard work paying off this season
blocks.text: It means a lot. I think I've done the work. I've worked very, very hard and very well this year, so super happy how everything is going on Tour. I'm enjoying my time on Tour and let's keep pushing to achieve bigger things in the future.

blocks.label: on his ambition to keep improving
blocks.text: But obviously, having played against the best players in the world, I see that if I keep improving and if I have ambition to be better every day, I think I can be a better player. That's what it's all about. I have been every day a little bit better and improving in all the things that I think I can be better in the future.

blocks.label: after his win over Jodar
blocks.text: Here the first set was a bit so-so. I was struggling a little bit, a bit of frustration. … A little bit of relief now.

blocks.label: on his first win after the opening loss to Shelton
blocks.text: It means a lot to me. It means a lot after a tough start. Of course, I played a great match against Ben, actually. Just unlucky.

blocks.label: on playing Zverev next
blocks.text: Well, it's going to be tough, of course. But I know that I can battle. I can go deep in the battle and I don't care about long matches. So I'm just not afraid. … I don't have anything to lose. I'm just coming to enjoy myself.

blocks.label: after his win over cobolli
blocks.text: He actually managed to do it quite well on the break points in the first set. There was one point where I could have done a tiny bit better, but other than that he was serving well. So I'm happy that I managed to stay tough and get the win.

blocks.label: on his serve on the fast indoor court
blocks.text: Yeah, I managed to serve well. It's a very fast indoor court, so the serve is important, and I managed to do it better than him today.

blocks.label: on his baseline game
blocks.text: I liked the way I was serving, but I feel like from the baseline, if I had just a tiny bit more rhythm, I could go for a bit more shots, I could maybe punish him a bit more on the short balls. But again, it doesn't matter. The most important thing is to win, and I'm happy to do it and I'm looking forward to the next matches.

blocks.label: on his best chance of beating Alcaraz
blocks.text: I think this court offers the best chance of beating Alcaraz. That doesn't mean you're going to manage it, because today he only lost four games. But in my opinion, it's in these conditions that you have the best chance of beating him, because you can get a few free points on serve and hit a few winners thanks to the speed of the surface. Which isn't easy against him, because he's probably the best mover in history, along with Novak Djokovic. You just have to try to play your best tennis and take your opportunities.

blocks.label: on the tournament format
blocks.text: Well, yes and no, because you can lose and still be in the tournament. So I would challenge that a bit, but the difference is that there is no other tournament in the world where you're going to play a top 10 player in the first match.

blocks.label: on continuing with Golubev next year
blocks.text: With Golubev we will continue next year too.

blocks.label: after his loss to Alcaraz On his ATP Finals debut
blocks.text: I had a great time for the whole hour. It's a fantastic experience to be here. Walking out onto the court is really special. It's a bit strange to walk out onto the court and play your first match against him of all people. Usually you face him in the final stages. In any case, everything here is really special.

blocks.label: on Alcaraz's level against him
blocks.text: He has moments where he's definitely Superman and he's playing pretty insane. You got to appreciate greatness.

blocks.label: on the 6-4 point and a year's work
blocks.text: The 6-4 point is literally why I put all that work in in the last year.

blocks.label: on winning a set 6-0
blocks.text: I wasn't thinking I was going to win it 6-0. I can't remember the last time I won a set 6-0, but I'll take it.

blocks.label: after his win over Tiafoe
blocks.text: I prepared for the match, tactically, really well. I tried to be really focused at the beginning, trying to know tactically what I have to do from the first point to the last one. I'm trying to push him and let him know that it's going to be a really great battle if he wants to go forward and if he wants to win. Today I felt like everything was working for me. I'm just really happy to start the tournament like this, and hopefully keep it going.

blocks.label: on feeling his best ever at this stage of the season
blocks.text: Never, to be honest. I would say this is the best I have felt so far in my career at this part of the season, which I'm really happy with. I have never experienced something like this, this year. It was unusual for me, having a lot of months off the competition at home. So that made me come here with a lot of energy, with a lot of ambition, and hungry for the matches, and I'm hungry for more.

blocks.label: on his near-perfect form at the ATP Finals
blocks.text: Sometimes I feel really comfortable. I feel like I'm better than the opponent in every aspect of the game. If I qualify to the semi-final or not, I think it's a great experience, a great week, getting experience. If the grade was a 9.8, that means I can improve it up to a ten. No, I don't feel unstoppable, but it is true that I notice everything is going in for me and that my opponent isn't hurting me. But there is still a lot ahead. We have the world number one, Zverev, and a Ben Shelton who is in great form. Let's see if I can keep up the level.

blocks.label: on his improving game on indoor courts
blocks.text: I've always said that I'm not bad on indoor courts. It's just that it seemed to me that other players were a bit better than me. It was just a matter of time, of gaining more experience, of understanding how I had to play on indoor courts. I think I'm almost there. I'm starting to understand how I should play indoors. I've gained more experience. Every time I play on this surface I also gain confidence. I'm really happy to show everyone that I can play great tennis here. I can hold my own against anyone with powerful, flat serves and shots, and be able to win those kinds of matches. I'm just happy to see that I'm reaching the level I always thought I could reach.

blocks.label: on his knee and how the injury changed him
blocks.text: The knee? I'm taking care of it, for now I'm moving well. The injury made me realise what's important, what's really important. When you realise that, everything comes easier for me, because I enjoy and I don't feel stressed on a tennis court, or most of the time I don't feel stressed on a tennis court, which means I can face the problems in a different way. More calm, relaxed, and I'm thinking: OK, I'm going to still try my best tennis, I'm going to still try what I have to do.

blocks.label: on his team banning golf during the season
blocks.text: Well, I can't play it yet, because my team won't let me. The first thing I'll do after the end of the season will probably be to play golf.

blocks.label: after his win over Fils
blocks.text: That was really intense, especially in the first set. I don't know that I've played that many rallies out there on tour on a court this fast. So it was physical, really physical. A tough contest. I was breathing hard after pretty much every point, and I'm excited to get started in a match like that. Everything wasn't perfect, but my overall level was good and I thought it was a great match I will be able to build on this week.

blocks.label: on the fast court conditions in Turin
blocks.text: The court is fast. Yes, very fast. They say Paris was one of the fastest courts of all time. I think that with the slight altitude here, the ball flies a bit more. In my opinion, the playing conditions are slightly faster than in Paris, but they remain comparable. It's quite close. It's nice to have a bit of continuity from one week to the next, playing on a fast hard court in Paris, then here in Turin. Last year, Paris was really slow, it was one of the slowest hard-court tournaments of the year, whereas in Turin, it's really fast.

blocks.label: on working with Ferrero alongside his father
blocks.text: It was great to have him alongside my father. They are two people who are hungry for success and who are enthusiastic. These past few days, we have already worked a lot, trying to improve every day. I am sure they will be satisfied with some of the things I did today and less satisfied with others. We are going to keep moving forward from there.

blocks.label: after his loss to Shelton
blocks.text: It's a shame that I started the third set with the handbrake slightly on. I'm staying positive ahead of the next matches.

blocks.label: on facing Rafael Jodar at the ATP Finals
blocks.text: I'll have to go after him and beat him. I'll have to be very positive in my head and have a good attitude. It won't be easy, that's for sure. He has beaten me twice this year, I have beaten him once. We'll see what happens. I'll have my chances, he'll have his.

blocks.label: after his first win at the Finals
blocks.text: It means a lot … Giving myself a little bit of momentum moving forward is huge. All the matches are really tough here, so it can be an uphill battle if you get behind early, and for me to get my first win here in front of this crowd is amazing.

blocks.label: on the intensity of the match
blocks.text: Really intense, especially the first set. The balls were a bit older that set. I don't know that I've played that many rallies out here on tour on a court this fast. So it was physical, really physical, tough contest. I was breathing hard after pretty much every point … My overall level was good and I thought it was a great match that I'll be able to build on this week.

blocks.label: on his new coaching team
blocks.text: It was awesome for me. Obviously, my box does look a little bit different now. Super excited. I think that I have some brilliant tennis minds in my corner, some great motivators, some guys who are hungry, excited to be out here, and we're a motivated team. Let's see what we can do this week and also in the future moving forward.

blocks.label: after his loss to Zverev
blocks.text: He handled the important points better than I did. I don't feel pressure, I try to enjoy it as much as possible.

blocks.label: on representing Spain at the Davis Cup Final 8
blocks.text: I still have this tournament and next week, Davis Cup as well. I think these two tournaments are very special for me, because representing my country in the Final 8 will be something unique. I'm very grateful and lucky to be part of the Team Spain.

blocks.label: after his win over Jodar
blocks.text: To start the tournament with a 6-4, 6-4 win is always very, very nice. It wasn't the perfect match, but I'm happy; it's a great start to the tournament for me. That was fun, wins always help, of course, and I hope that I can keep going like this.

blocks.label: on criticism of his record against top-10 players
blocks.text: No, because it's noise that you hear from the side. I don't really recognize that. I think I played a fantastic season. If you look at the record against the players that are here, who are now currently the eight best players in the world, I have a 6-2 record against them all. The top 10 this year has changed so much, and how the top 10 started and how the top 10 looks right now, it's such a big difference.

blocks.label: on his season and playing the ATP Finals
blocks.text: It's been a very good year for me. A lot of things that I've wanted to achieve I have achieved this year. But playing here you can never take it for granted.

blocks.label: after his opening win
blocks.text: Yeah, I think it was a solid match. I don't think it was perfect, but I think it was a very good start to the tournament … happy with the start, but I know I have to improve still.

blocks.label: on Nastase's stories
blocks.text: He had the best stories because he came from a generation where a sense of humor was still allowed, and he's not on social media, he's not on anything, so he just continued doing what he was doing 50 years ago or 30 years ago, and he's just a funny guy.

blocks.label: on the former world number ones
blocks.text: I think all of them have great stories.

blocks.label: after his opening win at the ATP Finals
blocks.text: I think it was a solid match. I don't think it was perfect, but I think it's a very good start to the tournament. With a 6-4, 6-4 win at the Nitto ATP Finals against a Top 8 player in the world, you take that, for sure. I'm happy with the start, but I know I have to improve still.

blocks.label: on the discontinued domestic abuse case against him
blocks.text: They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day. I don't know what translations you have, but that's what it means. Done. We move on. I never ever want to hear another question about the subject again. That goes out to everybody. First of all, this isn't that kind of interview. Secondly, you know that the accusations have been proven false? I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.

blocks.label: on returning to the ATP Finals
blocks.text: I am very happy to be back here. It doesn't matter how many times you have already taken part in this tournament. It is always a special honour to be among the eight best players in the world - Jannik Sinner excepted.

blocks.label: on focusing on his group, not Alcaraz
blocks.text: We shouldn't treat anyone with disrespect. I'm not thinking about Carlos at the moment. I'm thinking about these three young gentlemen here.

blocks.label: on his chances of winning the ATP Finals
blocks.text: Honestly, every year I think it could be the year, but this one maybe more so because of the results I've had indoors and because of how we're understanding the game on these courts. As I've said many times, the serve is a great weapon in these conditions and it's something I've improved over the last few weeks. I feel very comfortable with it. Maybe we're arriving in our best condition, especially mentally. We're fresh, very eager to face all the difficulties that may come up and very excited about this tournament.

blocks.label: on his knee taping and stomach discomfort
blocks.text: I would say I have just been playing a lot of matches in not too many days and they have been physically demanding matches.

blocks.label: on qualifying for his first ATP Finals
blocks.text: I am very happy to be here. It was a dream when I was a kid to be able to play the Finals at the end of the year. We all know it is the best eight players and it is such an honour to be here, next to these guys. It is my first year and I am going to try to enjoy it as much as possible. We have a strong group so I think it will be a lot of fun and a lot of battles.

blocks.label: on his childhood idol and mentor Gael
blocks.text: When I was a kid my idol was Gael. We are very close. He has always helped me a lot about everything on the court and off the court. He is a big brother to me, so he was one of my inspirations.

blocks.label: on his hopes of a first ATP Finals title
blocks.text: Every year I think this is going to be my year here.

blocks.label: on his upset stomach before the ATP Finals
blocks.text: I didn't even have breakfast this morning because I couldn't. I woke up with my stomach feeling a bit upset.

blocks.label: on his mental readiness after injury doubts
blocks.text: In the best condition, above all mentally … there were doubts about whether I would come back at one hundred percent.

blocks.label: on the ATP Finals field
blocks.text: Well, obviously the ATP Finals is the best eight players in the world.

blocks.label: on qualifying for and winning this tournament
blocks.text: It is a really important goal at the start of the year: to play the best, qualify and play this tournament. For me, it would be a massive success lifting this trophy, so I am just doing great practices to be ready to play a great tournament.

blocks.label: on approaching this season with confidence
blocks.text: I'm going to believe that I can do that, and I'm going to go this year with a lot of confidence. I'm going to go for it, for sure.

blocks.label: on the physical toll of a heavy match schedule
blocks.text: I would say I have just been playing a lot of matches in not too many days and they have been physically demanding matches. There are some problems that came up which are normal, I would say, for a tennis player. Right now I am just taking care of my preparation and I am feeling good.

blocks.label: on showing respect to everyone
blocks.text: I think we shouldn't disrespect anybody.

blocks.label: on his focus for the week ahead
blocks.text: So my focus is on them at the moment and then we see what will happen later in the week.
